t: For pay, allowances, individual clothing, subsistence, interest on deposits, gratuities, permanent change of station travel (including all expenses thereof for organizational movements), and expenses of temporary duty travel between permanent duty stations, for members of the Air Force on active duty (except members of reserve components provided for elsewhere), cadets, and aviation cadets; for members of the Reserve Officers’ Training Corps; and for payments pursuant to section 156 of Public Law 97–377, as amended (42 U.S.C. 402 note), and to the Department of Defense Military Retirement Fund, $28,052,826,000.

fable.w: This is a pure appropriations provision funding pay, allowances, and related expenses for Air Force military personnel. There is no tempting reading here: it involves no consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body, rulemaking, or right to sue, and no party outside the federal government takes part in any federal decision.
fable.s: for members of the Air Force on active duty (except members of reserve components provided for elsewhere), cadets, and aviation cadets

qwen_block.w: This section is an appropriations provision that authorizes funding for the pay, allowances, and travel expenses of military personnel. It does not involve any consultation, coordination, or decision-making process with parties outside the federal government. The actors involved are federal employees (Air Force members, cadets) and federal funds.
qwen_block.s: For pay, allowances, individual clothing, subsistence, interest on deposits, gratuities, permanent change of station travel (including all expenses thereof for organizational movements), and expenses of temporary duty travel between permanent duty stations, for members of the Air Force on active duty

opus.w: This section only sets aside $28,052,826,000 for Air Force pay, allowances, travel and related payments. No one outside the federal government is consulted, and there is no hearing, comment period, advisory committee or right to sue. Mentioning payments under another public law, or to the Military Retirement Fund, is just a funding category, not participation by outside parties.
opus.b: **Analysis:** Someone might read "payments pursuant to section 156 of Public Law 97–377" or "interest on deposits" as a process involving outsiders. That reading fails: this is a plain appropriation that funds Air Force military personnel costs. It describes no consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body or right to sue.

qwen_chat.w: This section is an appropriations clause authorizing funds for the pay, allowances, and travel expenses of federal military personnel and cadets. It does not involve consultation, coordination, or decision-making input from parties outside the federal government. Active-duty military members and cadets are considered part of the federal government structure, and the payment of their salaries is an internal administrative function, not public participation.
qwen_chat.s: For pay, allowances, individual clothing, subsistence, interest on deposits, gratuities, permanent change of station travel (including all expenses thereof for organizational movements), and expenses of temporary duty travel between permanent duty stations, for members of the Air Force on active duty (except members of reserve components provided for elsewhere), cadets, and aviation cadets; for members of the Reserve Officers’ Training Corps; and for payments pursuant to section 156 of Public Law 97–377, as amended (42 U.S.C. 402 note), and to the Department of Defense Military Retirement Fund, $28,052,826,000.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that "members of the Air Force" or "cadets" are outside the federal government and that paying them constitutes a form of participation or benefit application. However, active-duty military members and cadets are federal employees/officials, and the text is a standard appropriations clause authorizing funds for their compensation and travel, not a mechanism for public consultation, advisory input, or decision-making participation. The definition explicitly excludes applications for benefits and intra-governmental matters.
